title: OpenHands reliability benchmark — event-sourced persistence & delivery patterns
description: Evidence-backed summary of OpenHands (OSS) persistence model, workspace/sandbox semantics, event delivery path, incident coverage, transferable patterns and suggested minimal integration for durable artifact delivery.

openhands_features.how_openhands_implements_it: events directory (one JSON per event) + base_state.json snapshot with locking and atomic append
openhands_features.integration_gap: Workspace artifacts depend on workspace type; may need explicit copy-out for ephemeral Docker workspaces

openhands_features.how_openhands_implements_it: Pluggable workspaces: LocalWorkspace (host FS durable), Docker/Remote workspaces (ephemeral unless persistance_dir used)
openhands_features.integration_gap: Ensure persistence_dir is set or copy artifacts to durable store on finish

openhands_features.how_openhands_implements_it: Agent Server posts event batches to App Server; App Server persists then runs callback processors for side effects
openhands_features.integration_gap: No built-in end-to-end delivery ack tying FINISHED to external channel ack; callbacks are custom processors

openhands_features.how_openhands_implements_it: RemoteEventsList with reconcile() does REST initial fetch + WS subscribe and dedup by event id
openhands_features.integration_gap: Need to wire client-side reconcilers in bridges to avoid UI missed events

openhands_incidents.notes: EventLog + base_state snapshot enable deterministic replay.
Possible with LocalWorkspace; Docker/remote workspaces need explicit artifact copy-out to persistence_dir.
App Server callbacks do delivery but no end-to-end ACK guarantee; integrator must record delivery state.
RemoteEventsList.reconcile and EventLog index rebuilding provide concrete recovery primitives.

openhands_next_steps.action: Run conversation with DockerWorkspace that writes an ObservationEvent to persistence_dir, shut down workspace, verify artifact retained in persistence_dir.

Implement a lightweight callback processor that reads FINISH event, fetches artifact from EventLog, posts to Telegram with idempotency key (event.id) and stores delivery state (delivered/delivery_failed).
Add server-side post-FINISH validator that checks artifact existence and non-empty payload before allowing ConversationExecutionStatus -> FINISHED.

openhands_evidence.quote: Per-event files + base_state snapshot; autosave logic and persistence_dir docs.
append semantics, locking, id-to-index mapping and atomic writes.
ConversationExecutionStatus enum and FINISHED treated as terminal by run loop.
Webhook receiver persists events and dispatches callback processors.
RemoteEventsList merges/deduplicates by event id and has reconcile() to fetch missed events.

props.title: OpenHands reliability benchmark — event-sourced persistence & delivery patterns

props.content: OpenHands uses an append-only per-event file model with a base_state snapshot, making deterministic replay and idempotent read-back feasible. The platform separates execution from delivery: Agent Server pushes events to an App Server webhook which runs callback processors. Outbound channel delivery and guaranteed acknowledgements are integrator responsibilities. The evidence below cites exact OSS files for persistence, remote reconciliation, and webhook delivery logic.
